For he has said that the Jews will be deprived of bread and water, but the power of bread and the power of water. And we must desire to teach something like this. For when we encounter sacred words and read the divine Scriptures, then understand them, we receive the power of spiritual bread. For it is said, 'Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds out of the mouth of God.' Similarly, one should think about spiritual waters. The Jews, indeed, still have the bread and the water, for they are busy with the writings of Moses and read the law. However, since they do not understand anything, they do not have the power of bread or the power of water. For they have been given only the bare letter, which has an opinion about bread and water, but does not nourish them in any way towards spiritual well-being. And the Scripture will testify through Paul, 'For until this day, whenever Moses is read, a veil lies on their heart, not being revealed, that it is done away with in Christ.' And in another way, we say that they have been deprived of the power of bread and the power of water from the Jewish synagogue. And the word is mystical. For we who have been called to sanctification through faith have the bread that comes from heaven, that is, Christ, or his body. And if someone were to ask what the power of this bread is, we say that it is life-giving. For it gives life to the world.

We approach similarly the grace through holy baptism, which sanctifies us, saying the power of water is the removal of sins, spiritual rebirth, into conformity to Christ. And besides these, it has a bold entrance into the kingdom of heaven. For if one is not born of water and spirit, they cannot enter the kingdom of God. The Jews lack these goods. They do not have the power of bread, that is, the life-giving power in Christ. They do not have the power of water. Unforgiven sin remains with them. They will not enter the kingdom of heaven, having dishonored Christ who brings them in. They did not believe him when he said, 'I am the way and the door.' He takes away both the giant and the strong. Then who is the giant and who is the strong? I think the giant is the one who has come to the language of spiritual power, and the strong is the one who has been humbled and overcome by the superiority in it. For each of us has been given a measure of God's grace.
pass_b_english: The spiritual nourishment that comes from God is not just about physical bread and water, but about the power of bread and the power of water. This is what we must desire to teach, for when we encounter sacred words and read the divine Scriptures, we receive the power of spiritual bread. As it is written, 'Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds out of the mouth of God.'

The Jews, however, still cling to the physical bread and water, busy with the writings of Moses and reading the law. But since they do not understand the spiritual significance, they do not have the power of bread or the power of water. The Scripture testifies to this through Paul, who says that a veil lies on their heart when they read Moses, and that it is done away with in Christ. We, on the other hand, who have been called to sanctification through faith, have the bread that comes from heaven, which is Christ, or his body. And the power of this bread is life-giving, for it gives life to the world.

We approach the grace of holy baptism, which sanctifies us and gives us the power to remove sins and be reborn spiritually, conforming us to Christ. This baptism also gives us a bold entrance into the kingdom of heaven, as Jesus said, 'Unless one is born of water and spirit, they cannot enter the kingdom of God.' The Jews, however, lack this gift, for they do not have the power of bread, which is the life-giving power in Christ, nor do they have the power of water, which is necessary for spiritual rebirth.

As a result, unforgiven sin remains with them, and they will not enter the kingdom of heaven, having dishonored Christ who brings them in. They did not believe him when he said, 'I am the way and the door.' Christ takes away both the giant and the strong, and we must understand who these are. The giant is the one who has come to the language of spiritual power, and the strong is the one who has been humbled and overcome by the superiority in it. Each of us has been given a measure of God's grace, as the apostle Paul said, 'I want all men to be like me.'
